# Machine-owned mission

The user explicitly requires the machine itself to rebuild the machinery and
perform the mathematical campaigns. The supervisor supplies requirements,
resource boundaries, primary-paper identities, independent review, and versioning;
it must not supply mathematical answers or prewritten proof recipes.

## Construction

Read docs/DESIGN.md in full. Starting from this empty project, implement the
research system and its formal foundations. The actual proposer is Codex with
gpt-6-astra. Develop executable code, not just an architectural report. Keep
problem contracts explicit, and separate mathematical truth from usefulness
and novelty. There are no artificial research levels or lemma-count rewards.
Kolmogorov/description-length measures are audit-only and may not affect
curiosity, scheduling, admission, or switch approval.

The action space must support literature search, Python/Sage/GAP experiments
when available, representation changes, conjectures, Lean proofs/refutations,
component gluing, and proposed code changes. Unavailable tools are capability
failures. Experiments and retrieved text are not Lean theorems. Provisional
exploration remains flexible; persistent certified self-rewrites require the
whole-continuation proof, an operational connection, exact bindings, and costs.

Construct and test the proof-admission boundary and the reflective execution
model. Formally define the gluing maps and prove the preservation properties
actually used. Demonstrate a concrete installed self-rewrite tied to its checked
semantics. Explicitly report model assumptions and implementation limits.
Do not call a benchmark improvement, abstract implication, changed prompt, or
untested gate a full Gödel machine. Never introduce sorry, admissions, hidden
axioms, native-evaluation axioms, or a postulated global self-soundness theorem.
Use ordinary Mathlib axioms only, and independently audit English versus Lean.

## First mathematical campaign

Takashi Agoh, An Intrinsic Factor of an Alternating Sum Involving Certain
Rational Functions, INTEGERS 26 (2026), A9.
Primary paper: https://math.colgate.edu/~integers/aa9/aa9.pdf
DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.18154119

Retrieve the original source, inventory its statements and hypotheses, choose
and formalize the paper exercise through the machine's own agenda, reproduce
the relevant proofs or rigorously identify errors, and audit statement meaning.
Record what has and has not been established. Do not replace universal claims
with finite scans or silently change their hypotheses.

## Subsequent conjecture campaign

S. J. Evans, A. P. Veselov, B. Winn, Arithmetic and Geometry of Markov polynomials.
Primary paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.14882
Publisher: https://armj.math.stonybrook.edu/Articles/250708-Winn/index.html
Target: Conjecture 6.3, coefficient log-concavity of Markov polynomials.

After the first campaign, attack this conjecture using the rebuilt machine.
Read and audit the exact target before formalizing it. The machine chooses its
own lemmas, representations, literature, experiments, and proof attempts.
The aim is a serious, reproducible attack, not an invented claim of resolution.

## Provenance and workflow

All generated code, proofs, and experiments must carry machine provenance.
Use short, durable checkpoints so interruption does not erase work. Preserve
failed attempts and explicit remaining obligations. The supervisor will make
local Git commits; do not read or modify Git internals, push, or contact people.
Remain inside this project and the supplied third-party toolchain/dependencies.
Do not read older project archives, previous-session transcripts, retired build
outputs, or predecessor proofs. No solution from an earlier version is supplied.
# Clean bootstrap of a Gödel machine for mathematical research

This document is a design specification for a fresh construction. It supplies
no previous implementation, mathematical results, proof scripts, or successful
research strategies. It distinguishes an adaptive mathematical researcher, a
formally certified continuation model, and an executable Gödel machine. A
checked theorem about an abstract model does not by itself establish that an
implementation realizes that model or that the model describes future Astra
calls.

The intended system uses a flexible LLM proposer, reusable mathematical
components, and explicit gluing interfaces. It can search literature, conduct
computational experiments, change representations, formulate conjectures, and
attempt proofs and refutations. Its scientific objective is problem-specific.
Kolmogorov-style measurements are audit data, not a universal objective or an
automatic curiosity reward.

## What the original construction requires

Schmidhuber's target compares a proposed switch with continuing the entire
incumbent program, including future proof search and later self-modifications.
The machine and environment are axiomatized. Checking and installation take
time; the switch protocol binds a target time and can reject a late proof.
The resulting optimality claim is relative to the utility, assumptions, and
incumbent search, rather than an oracle maximum over all programs. The paper
also permits a nondegradation target, different initial searchers, and changes
to utility code justified by the previous utility. Its mathematical example
rewards the first verified proof or disproof by the reciprocal of elapsed time.
Useful changes may be unprovable in the chosen system or undiscoverable within
available resources. These requirements come from §§2.4, 3.2, 4, 5, and 6 of
[the original paper](https://arxiv.org/pdf/cs/0309048).

The architecture and acceptance criteria below are our engineering proposal.
They are not claims that the original paper supplies a working implementation
for Lean, an opaque external LLM, or this mathematical research problem.

## The problem contract, rather than manufactured levels

ARC supplies an external environment with explicit levels and validated
completion conditions. The mathematics application has no corresponding
natural sequence of levels. Numbering accepted lemmas does not create one.

A run therefore starts with an explicit, versioned problem contract:

- An exact root proposition, its intended English meaning, and permitted
  assumptions. Resolution may mean a checked proof or checked negation.
- A declared utility or preference over research outcomes and their costs.
  This is supplied for the problem, not inferred from a theorem counter.
- Resource limits and a cost interpretation: abstract computation steps,
  elapsed time, provider usage, or separately recorded quantities.
- The environment assumptions under which prospective comparisons are made.
- Admission and completion rules that a proposal cannot redefine.

A root-resolution/time objective is one reasonable instance, not a default
definition of all mathematical value. Intermediate results can have value
when the contract says how that value is assessed. If such an assessment is
human or heuristic, its status must remain visible.

Truth, relevance, novelty, and expected usefulness are separate properties.
A kernel-checked lemma establishes its proposition. A separately checked
reduction can establish its logical connection to the root. Neither fact
alone establishes historical novelty or how likely the lemma is to help.
Even an implication into the root can have an impossible antecedent.
Experimental evidence may change the agenda without closing a formal task.

No part of admission, root closure, scheduling, or persistent rewrite approval
may quietly depend on source length, compression ratio, or a claimed estimate
of Kolmogorov complexity. Audit measurements can still describe reuse and
representation costs. Their production must have ordinary resource accounting.

## Open research actions and explicit evidence

The proposer needs an extensible action interface rather than a fixed menu of
prewritten mathematical recipes. Concrete capabilities can include:

| Action | Output | What the output establishes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Literature search and source reading | Queries, primary URLs, passages, retrieval times | What a source reports; not a Lean theorem |
| Python, Sage, or GAP experiment | Program, inputs, versions, outputs, costs | A reproducible computation under recorded semantics |
| Representation proposal | Definitions, maps, examples, desired transport laws | A proposed viewpoint until its laws are checked |
| Proof or refutation | Exact target, proof term, dependencies, kernel receipt | The proposition admitted by the proof gate |
| Component attachment | Boundary, bindings, adapters, checked obligations | The specific preservation properties proved |
| Search strategy proposal | Diagnosis, next actions, resource allocation | Provisional guidance consumed by the controller |
| Persistent code rewrite | Exact replacement, state migration, switch certificate | Only the certified comparison and preservation claims |

An adapter may expose a new experimental language or mathematical interface
without giving the proposer unrestricted host authority. The broker enforces
capabilities and records failures. An unavailable Sage or GAP installation is
a capability failure, not evidence against a conjecture. Network failures,
timeouts, and malformed responses similarly remain transport or execution
outcomes rather than mathematical refutations.

Finite scans do not prove universal claims. Exact counterexamples can become
formal refutations after the relevant witness and hypotheses are independently
checked. External theorems may be recorded as explicit assumptions when a
contract permits that treatment; retrieved text must not add hidden axioms.

## Exploration must not require a switch proof at every step

The incumbent research policy may already authorize broad exploratory actions,
task invention, hypothesis changes recorded as new tasks, and provisional
strategy updates. Choosing such an action is ordinary execution of that policy.
It need not first prove that its next web query or experiment is globally best.

A persistent replacement of the controller or its search procedure is a
different event. It requires either the full switch gate described below or an
explicitly labeled experimental branch that makes no certified-improvement
claim. Successful tests alone must not promote that branch to a proved switch.

This separation prevents two failures: an inert system unable to explore until
it has solved its own research problem, and an unrestricted self-editor whose
ordinary strategy changes are advertised as Gödel-certified improvements.
Exploration remains flexible within the current contract and capability limits.

## Operational semantics and the whole continuation

The formal machine state should contain executable controller and proof-search
code, persistent research data, the archive and agenda, resource state, pending
requests, and enough environment history to interpret future actions. Program
code must be inspectable data. A semantics must explain how each instruction,
external response, and accepted rewrite changes that state.

Crucially, the incumbent continuation includes its own future proposals,
verification attempts, discoveries, and switches. A comparison against a
frozen policy that is forbidden to improve does not compare against the actual
incumbent. The replacement continuation must likewise include its subsequent
behavior, not just its first apparently beneficial action.

One conceptual interface is:

```text
step       : Program × State × Input -> Transition
run        : Program × State × Environment -> Trace
evaluate   : ProblemContract × Trace -> Utility
install    : Candidate × State -> InstallationTrace × State
```

This interface is a specification sketch, not an executable API or a proof.
In a stochastic instance, `run` induces a distribution and `evaluate` supplies
an expected value when the required measurability and integrability hold.
In a robust instance, comparisons quantify over declared environment behaviors.
The implementation must connect these objects to the bytes it actually runs.

## The switch obligation and a common time baseline

For contract `C`, model `mu`, incumbent `p`, candidate `q`, and decision state
`s`, the intended strict obligation is:

```text
V(C, mu, install-and-continue(q, s))
  > V(C, mu, continue-whole-machine(p, s)).
```

Both sides use the same contract, environmental assumptions, and decision
baseline. The comparison may instead be nonstrict when that is the declared
rule. This is a semantic statement about complete continuations; it is not a
claim that both values must be computed exactly before a proof can be found.

Search already performed before this baseline is sunk on both branches. Do not
charge it twice or selectively subtract it from the incumbent. Validation and
installation still to be performed must be included. If final validation has
already occurred, its elapsed time instead appears in the new state and the
remaining lifetime. A certificate proved from an earlier snapshot must justify
transport to the installation state or be checked against an appropriate future
deadline and invariant. Simply adding a measured cost to an old inequality is
insufficient when the remaining opportunity to solve the problem has changed.

A switch receipt must bind the contract and model, incumbent and replacement
code, exact state or proved state invariant, migration, cost interpretation,
deadline, certificate target, and independent verification artifacts. Reject
changed bindings and stale deadlines. Hashes bind recorded bytes; they are not
proofs that Python or operating-system execution realizes the Lean semantics.

Changing runtime reward code cannot redefine the standard used to approve the
change. Representation changes to the objective require a transport proof.
A new scientific objective requires a new explicit contract; silently weakening
the root or environmental assumptions is not an improvement.

## Opaque models and self-reference

Astra is an external proposer with unknown internals and no assumed success
probability. Treat its responses and delays as environmental inputs. A measured
acceptance rate, benchmark gain, or confidence estimate does not establish its
future response law. A Bayesian comparison is conditional on its declared
model; a robust comparison must actually quantify over the stated model class.
Neither should be reported as an unconditional real-world guarantee.

One promising certificate pattern proves preservation for every corresponding
response stream while reducing internal work. However, corresponding streams
require justification: an API or web service can depend on request time and
history. Faster execution need not receive the same responses. The environment
contract or a coupling argument must support that correspondence.

Encoding one's own code is not the same as proving unrestricted soundness of
one's own proof system. A sufficiently strong consistent theory cannot simply
adopt its own unrestricted reflection principle. This is the relevant obstacle
discussed in [Yudkowsky and Herreshoff's primary analysis](https://intelligence.org/files/TilingAgentsDraft.pdf).
Our design uses particular checked proofs and concrete simulations; it must
not introduce an unchecked `SelfSound` axiom to discharge future correctness.
The reference kernel, admission semantics, and runtime bridge are explicit
trust boundaries. Faster implementations need preservation certificates against
that reference; replacing the reference by a candidate's assertion of trust
does not prove preservation.

## Gluing and representation transport

A finite-name attachment can have a unique-extension property for compatible
maps. Proving such a restricted pushout would not establish semantic
conservativity of arbitrary source edits or dependent Lean declarations.

The design requires typed interfaces: declarations, hypotheses, dependencies,
interpretations, and any renaming or substitution. A new cell must discharge
its assumptions from the accepted context. Context attachment should preserve
the original models and hence their consequences. Sequential attachment must
preserve this fact, including when later cells reuse earlier checked cells.

A representation adapter must preserve the observations or predicates needed
by its consumer. When a representation identifies two objects that a target
property distinguishes, no exact adapter can recover that property from the
representation alone. Such collisions should become explicit failed obligations
or counterexamples, not be hidden by successful tests on a small sample.

For code components, coherent signatures are only the beginning: a simulation
must connect glued implementations to their specification and cost model.
Gluing correctness then supports a switch proof; it does not imply usefulness.
The terms “cofibered” and “cofibrant” require a specified category, structure,
and associated laws. Fiber-respecting maps and injective context embeddings
alone do not establish a model-category cofibration or a Grothendieck opfibration.

## Milestones and acceptance criteria

1. **Problem-directed exploration.** Run the configurable contract and action
   broker with Astra proposals, real feedback, explicit evidence classes, and
   cost accounting. Demonstrate a nonproof action affecting a later research
   decision. Synthetic fixtures test the protocol; they do not demonstrate
   autonomous mathematical discovery.
2. **Semantic foundations.** Prove conservative context attachment, representation
   transport conditions, and continuation comparisons with explicit costs.
   A bounded trace/Bellman model is a useful verified instance. State exactly
   which horizon, response relation, and policy class it quantifies over.
3. **Reflective executable bridge.** Provide executable code semantics with code
   in state and future switching included. Prove or explicitly audit the bridge
   from concrete controller transitions, time accounting, and state migration
   to that semantics. Merely supplying an arbitrary value function fails this
   milestone. A finite table or a single prescribed trajectory also fails it.
4. **A concrete certified self-change.** Produce a candidate, an independently
   checked whole-continuation certificate, and an actual guarded installation.
   A semantics-preserving optimization with a net cost improvement is a useful
   first case. Its proof must cover future switches and installation overhead,
   not merely reproduce the outcomes in the selection benchmark.
5. **General search and reuse.** Let the proposer invent components, adapters,
   and candidate rewrites. A fair proof enumerator can supply completeness
   relative to a calculus if required; an LLM alone supplies no such guarantee.
   Neither option requires a Kolmogorov reward or manufactured task levels.

Completing a finite, specified instance does not establish a switch guarantee
for arbitrary unbounded research or an unmodeled LLM. A generic theorem whose
hypotheses assume the very utility comparison at issue is a framework, not an
independent proof that a concrete rewrite improves the researcher.

## Adversarial examples and regression requirements

The audit must include passing examples and failures with one condition removed:

- A valid reduction versus an unrelated true lemma falsely credited as root
  completion; a refutation of the exact goal versus a changed-hypothesis target.
- A numerical pattern versus a kernel-checked universal statement; a missing
  experimental tool versus a negative mathematical result.
- A compatible attachment versus a conflicting binding, new unproved assumption,
  omitted dependency, circular cell dependency, or lossy representation adapter.
- A cheaper equivalent continuation versus one whose installation overhead
  removes the gain, or whose earlier deadline defeats the promised outcome.
- A full incumbent that later finds a better rewrite versus a comparator that
  artificially disables that future search; the latter certificate must fail.
- Identical objective semantics versus a replacement that edits the reward,
  root, model assumptions, or verifier to manufacture apparent improvement.
- A correctly bound certificate versus changed candidate bytes, changed state,
  stale time, mismatched model, forged receipt, or replayed old approval.
- An exploratory strategy revision versus a persistent executable rewrite;
  exploratory authorization must not silently authorize the latter.
- Different complexity-audit values with identical research inputs: admission,
  scheduling, and switch decisions remain identical. Logging costs may differ
  only when the measurement operation itself genuinely differs.

Formal negative examples should exhibit the missing mathematical hypothesis,
not just malformed JSON. Runtime tests should exercise actual gate boundaries.
Successful tests are evidence about implementation behavior, not a substitute
for the semantic connection required by milestone 3.

## Machine-authored bootstrap and experimental status

The initial input is this design, the user-selected research problem descriptions
and primary-source references, pinned Lean/Mathlib metadata, and a minimal launch
and containment interface. The machine must create the new implementation,
formal statements, proofs, experiments, tests, and documentation. The supervisor
provides execution, resource limits, evidence retention, and independent audit;
it must not insert mathematical solution steps or implement the research engine
on the machine's behalf while describing the result as machine-authored.

A bootstrap cannot claim that its first controller edits are already authorized
by a Gödel switch theorem whose verifier and executable semantics it has yet to
construct. Those edits run in an explicitly experimental workspace under the
user's authorization to rebuild. Compilation, tests, and subsequent independent
checks can validate aspects of the resulting code. They do not retroactively
prove that the bootstrap's sequence of edits was utility-optimal.

The machine must report separate transitions between these statuses:

- **Experimental bootstrap:** code generation and exploration without an
  installed whole-continuation switch certificate.
- **Checked research:** concrete proof objects pass an independently validated
  admission boundary; individual accepted propositions may be reported exactly.
- **Verified model:** formal theorems describe an explicitly stated machine and
  environment model, with the implementation bridge still separately identified.
- **Certified persistent switch:** an actual installation passes the bound,
  independently checked certificate and execution-bridge obligations above.

These labels are evidence classes, not mathematical levels, utility scores,
or a requirement that all components progress in a fixed order. A machine can
produce a valid mathematical theorem during an experimental bootstrap. That
alone certifies neither its surrounding engine nor its future self-modifications.
Machine-generated reports of success remain claims until their evidence is
independently checked; a self-authored test harness cannot certify itself by
printing a successful receipt.

## Clean-input and provenance acceptance checklist

Before the rebuilding proposer runs, independently verify the following:

- Historical source, draft implementations, proof scripts, discoveries, tests,
  experiments, transcripts, and run receipts are archived for the user outside
  the proposer's readable filesystem boundary. They are not bootstrap inputs.
- A Git archive preserves the historical work without exposing its object store
  or archive branch to the proposer. Deleting the working tree while leaving
  `git show` access to earlier solutions does not establish a clean boundary.
- No historical project `.olean`, generated module, cached proof expression,
  database, notebook output, or task-specific package supplies previous results.
  A pinned standard Lean/Mathlib installation is a declared dependency, not
  evidence of a newly created theorem.
- The proposer begins with a fresh conversation. Old assistant summaries,
  hidden solution files, previous success reports, and strategy suggestions
  are not inherited through its prompt, tools, environment, or resume state.
- Task inputs identify the selected publication or conjecture and the required
  outcome. They do not include previously found witnesses, lemmas, reductions,
  or successful representations. Public primary sources remain legitimate
  research inputs and their actual use is recorded.
- The run records an input manifest, hashes, toolchain pins, capabilities,
  workspace boundary, initial prompt, model identity, and resource limits.
  Archived historical objects and fresh generated objects remain distinguishable.
- All new code and mathematical artifacts are traceable to machine actions.
  Any later human correction, imported result, or boundary exception is recorded
  explicitly and narrows the corresponding autonomy or clean-input claim.
- Generated artifacts cannot overwrite supervisor-owned launch rules, hidden
  archives, independent validation tools, evidence manifests, or contract inputs.
  Proposed changes to those components remain candidates for separate review.

A prompt requesting that the proposer ignore readable historical answers is a
behavioral instruction, not enforced clean isolation. If filesystem isolation
is unavailable, report that limitation rather than claiming an enforced clean
run. The archive must remain recoverable by the user; cleaning the proposer
workspace does not authorize loss of the preserved historical work.

## What this specification does not yet establish

No implementation, kernel-checked result, certified controller rewrite, or
resolution of either selected research task is established by this document.
The machine must construct and test the machinery and supply the corresponding
evidence. A general continuation theorem, a useful research result, and a full
executable Gödel switch are separate achievements with separate obligations.

The absence of inherited answers does not establish historical originality:
claims of novelty still require a literature audit. Failed searches, timeouts,
and unfinished formalizations remain incomplete work, not evidence that the
mathematical target is false or unprovable.
# Version 2: discussion trace and acceptance obligations

Supervisor requirements record, 2026-10-17. This document supplies methodology and review criteria, not mathematical answers. The separate Codex/gpt-6-astra builder must author implementation and formal foundations. Coverage in a document is not implementation; a test is not a proof of a broader guarantee.

## Latest instructions take precedence

1. Finish the new harness, retracing the discussion and connecting the whole loop to the newly added methodology.
2. Audit the integrated source and its claim/evidence correspondence BEFORE the next validation run. Earlier construction test logs remain historical; they do not validate later changes.
3. After that audit, run meaningful machinery tests and report results and remaining limitations.
4. WAIT for the user's explicit OK before ANY fresh Markov log-concavity research, live Markov obligation curation, or live Markov canary. The stopped old campaign stays stopped. Do not activate a study while completing this task.
5. Work in math_gkm, not collatz. Retain old results, research logs, and reproducibility artifacts in version control/public archive; do not feed them to fresh research arms.

## Authority and interpretation

User requirements include the independent machine-owned proposer, autonomous action choice, construction by the machine, a serious Goedel-machine foundation, visible cofibrant/cofibered gluing, audit-only Kolmogorov measures, no artificial mathematical levels, broad tools, preservation/reproducibility, four approved exploration/strategy steps, fresh matched comparison, and the latest remaining-goal-relative complexity discussion.

The four approved steps are: competing research hypotheses; mathematical transfer evaluation; delayed benefit over episodes; and strategy changes as objects of fair experiments. Specific data structures, numbers of rounds, choice of fixed-panel coding, or review thresholds are implementation proposals and must be labeled as such. No universal score follows from the discussion. A finite evaluation cannot establish whole-continuation optimality.

The latest complexity proposal is interpreted as the remaining proof burden of a fixed goal relative to acquired knowledge. The goal statement is already known. Shortening its name or introducing an abbreviation is not evidence of easier proof. Measured encodings are computable proxies, not minimal Kolmogorov complexities. The user did not revoke the earlier audit-only constraint.

## Required connected research loop

A versioned exact problem contract enters the actual runner. The runner retains competing hypotheses, asks its own proposer for a prospective trial, records the chosen uncertainty/outcomes and episode horizon before execution, performs the chosen research action, records actual evidence, checks any asserted mathematical result and its premises, checks component attachment and representation transport where used, updates explicit remaining obligations, evaluates transfer/capability retention on a fair comparison, reviews the episode, tests any proposed policy change, records the selection with reasons and costs, then constructs the next request from the updated state. Stop, interruption and recovery must preserve that sequence without fabricating a result or repeating an uncertain action.

The description/proof-burden audit observes the same bound snapshots and costs through a one-way channel. Its values and derived proxies do not enter admission, action selection, scheduling, or policy-change acceptance. Mathematical reductions and checked transfer can be research evidence independently of their audit sizes.

Every edge needs a concrete producer, durable artifact, consumer, invariant and verification example. A callable helper or unused CLI command does not establish that an edge participates in the running loop.

## Requirement matrix

| ID | Requirement and acceptance evidence |
| --- | --- |
| O1 | Own external Codex/Astra proposer, distinct from this session. Persist actual model invocation, inputs, role, outputs, usage and elapsed time. Supervisor reviews/operates/versions but supplies no proof recipe. |
| O2 | Autonomous broad action choice: primary literature, Python and available Sage/GAP, numerical experiments, representations, conjectures, proofs/refutations, component attachment, strategy and executable-change proposals. Capability failures stay operational observations. |
| O3 | Explicit exact root/English meaning/assumptions/cost preference. No universal scalar usefulness function, manufactured levels, lemma-count reward or forced parameter-case sequence. Truth, relevance, novelty, usefulness and costs remain distinct. |
| P1 | Persistent competing obstacle/capability/strategy hypotheses with identities, alternatives, reasons and artifact-bound evidence. The next request genuinely uses this state. |
| P2 | Full prospective commitment: selected hypothesis/claim, uncertainty, alternatives, outcome checks, consequences for later choice, episode horizon and resource reservation are recorded before execution. Changed plans require a new explicit event, not retrospective rewriting. Applies to ordinary and comparison branches. |
| P3 | Bounded question/representation invention remains possible before an immediate reduction to the root is known. Lack of immediate payoff is not refutation. |
| P4 | Multiround episodes retain commitments and delayed use links across invocations. Review at a predetermined horizon, with explicit continuation budgets and no free planning/restarts. |
| M1 | A verified theorem is a proof of the exact claimed proposition under the allowed premise closure. Compilation/replay and printed reports alone must not conceal an additional assumption. Reject sorry/admit, unapproved axioms and native-evaluation axioms under this contract. |
| M2 | Root closure requires a closed proof of the pinned root or its exact negation, fresh checked artifacts, allowed axioms and the independent English/source correspondence audit. Partial results, scans, weaker normalization, finite cases and failed searches never close the root. |
| M3 | Checked relevance can be a reduction from explicit residual obligations to the unchanged goal, or a checked equivalence/transport. Record all residual assumptions; a tautological reduction or impossible antecedent is not demonstrated simplification. |
| G1 | Typed gluing is operationally visible: component premises, interface, interpretation/renaming, dependencies and transport laws are explicit; consumers actually use the checked maps/laws. A list of compatible names or three disconnected true propositions is insufficient. |
| G2 | Record the exact conservative-attachment/pushout/fiber/cofibration structure and laws actually formalized. Do not call arbitrary injective maps cofibrations or a symbol union a semantic pushout. Preserve earlier accepted results under attachment; test omitted premises and incompatible/lossy maps. |
| T1 | Independent held-out structural obligations are selected and frozen before the relevant comparison. Preserve selection provenance and withhold answers. The machine, not this session, selects mathematical tasks. No retrospective task invention to justify observed success. |
| T2 | Before/after continuations start from the same relevant state and face the SAME mathematical tasks/hypotheses/source semantics with equal adaptation allowances. The old solver may prove a task without the new component. |
| T3 | Separate task success from actual use of a newly acquired component. Bind used declarations and bodies to the frozen version; adaptation cannot substitute a different component. Changes only to comments or unrelated declarations do not establish use of new mathematics. |
| T4 | Distinguish bounded valid non-solution from missing output, invalid premises, source mismatch, interrupted validation or unavailable tools. An invalid comparison cannot establish improvement. Dependency use is not causal indispensability. Include matched ablations where feasible, with explicit scope. |
| T5 | Retain old proof/source capabilities and check regression coverage. State whether all previously accepted declarations or only a fixed suite are protected. Branches need the claimed retained context; do not promise history they cannot read. |
| S1 | Machine proposes search/memory/allocation/reassessment changes; actual separate reviewer/selector roles consume checked records. Trial incumbent and candidate over matched multiround continuations; charge planning, evaluation, installation and failures. A prose recommendation alone cannot authorize a change. |
| S2 | Installed experimental policy changes feed the next actual research request. Keep the baseline faithful to its declared incumbent policy; do not silently give it the new policy-selection machinery and still call it the old control. |
| S3 | Executable changes remain a supported proposal type, separately versioned and tested under an explicit experimental construction mode or checked installation path. Four editable prompt fields alone do not fulfill the original persistent executable self-change requirement. |
| D1 | Goedel obligation compares install-and-continue(candidate) against the WHOLE incumbent continuation, including future discoveries and self-changes, with common state/time/model/cost assumptions. A bounded policy experiment is not this theorem. |
| D2 | Actual transitions/receipts/state migration/code versions must connect to the stated semantics. Preserve separate statuses: experimental harness, checked mathematics, verified model, certified executable switch. A Lean model theorem alone does not prove Python/OS/LLM realization. |
| D3 | Keep the concrete certified-change and running-code bridge obligations explicit and active where not discharged. Do not assume global self-soundness, favorable future LLM behavior or the desired improvement as an unproved premise. A disclaimer records a gap; it does not complete it. |
| K1 | Observe remaining-proof burden relative to prior knowledge plus new proved components; do not equate goal-string length or total source storage with that quantity. Define what expressing/translating the goal means using checked reductions/interfaces and explicit residual tasks. |
| K2 | Use frozen, versioned encoding/reference tasks and paired old/new measurements on the SAME data/goal. Account for introduced definitions, adapters, connecting proofs and shared costs, so abbreviations cannot create a free apparent drop. Keep unrelated growing workload separate. |
| K3 | Save every scheduled checkpoint, raw measures, scope/encoding versions and cumulative cost, including unfavorable points. Plot actual data with change markers; allow flat, rising, irregular or insufficient data. Do not manufacture or require a sawtooth. |
| K4 | Unknown goal proof complexity stays unknown. A searched proof gives only the stated measured result/upper bound, and failed bounded search gives no mathematical lower bound. Reuse/transfer is evidence of direction, not a guarantee. Exploration need not reduce every per-step proxy. |
| K5 | Audit-only measurements and derived proxies cannot alter admission, proposals, allocation, selection, or goal closure. Verify invariance for changed audit records. Honest observer costs may be recorded; data/results are not fed back through summaries or role files. |
| C1 | Fresh matched baseline and exploration arms: identical clean mathematical seed, target, model/tools/dependencies and declared resource allowance; no old project lemmas, agendas, reports, cached project objects or other-arm results. Old campaign is archival evidence, not the matched control. |
| C2 | Record all initial inputs and common clean-start adjustments, dependency/tool identities and implemented access boundaries. Literature is allowed, but old project archives are not permitted research inputs. Do not claim absence of model pretraining knowledge. |
| C3 | Charge all extra roles/branches/planning/failures and disclose common setup overhead. Record actual provider usage without inventing token/cost equivalence. State ordering/provider drift, early stops, budget exhaustion and replication limits. |
| C4 | The original Agoh-then-Markov campaign order and results remain historical provenance; no claim those exercises were freshly rerun. Make the harness reusable for explicit problem contracts rather than silently replacing the fixed Markov goal. New Markov activation is currently awaiting user OK. |
| R1 | Durable versioned checkpoints and explicit recovery for interruption at every transition, including job creation before active-state recording. No duplicate uncertain actions, vanished receipts, unlocked overlap, or resolved goal reverting to open. |
| R2 | Preserve necessary source, tests, fixtures, pins, protocols, evidence and reproduction instructions in Git/public archive. Local compiler cleanup must not remove necessary archived inputs or research artifacts. No old work is purged during this revision. |
| R3 | Source audit precedes the next test run. Tests must exercise the entire connected cycle, actual Lean checks with positive/missing-condition examples, strategy change reaching the next request, stop/recovery, identical-seed comparison and audit-only separation. Bind results to exact tested source hashes. |
| R4 | No live Markov researcher, curator, canary or study launch before the user's explicit OK after the harness report. Test the machinery with clearly labeled neutral fixtures; no mathematical progress claims from them. |

## First-candidate disposition

The first separate builder has produced substantial executable study machinery, but this record does not approve it. Independent reviews found incomplete prospective-plan binding, comparison/provenance issues, a concrete allowed-premise check error, and an audit that initially measured source storage rather than conditional proof burden. Parts of the candidate are still changing. The original Goedel/gluing execution obligations also need explicit connection to the new loop, not just references to the original design.

The existing old Markov run remains stopped and publicly archived. Nothing here supplies a mathematical strategy or activates new Markov work. The next builder must produce a requirement-to-code/evidence/status mapping, implement missing integrated paths, state unresolved formal obligations precisely, and provide an audit checkpoint before executing its revised test suite.

  experimental tool versus a negative mathematical result.
- A compatible attachment versus a conflicting binding, new unproved assumption,
  omitted dependency, circular cell dependency, or lossy representation adapter.
- A cheaper equivalent continuation versus one whose installation overhead
  removes the gain, or whose earlier deadline defeats the promised outcome.
- A full incumbent that later finds a better rewrite versus a comparator that
  artificially disables that future search; the latter certificate must fail.
- Identical objective semantics versus a replacement that edits the reward,
  root, model assumptions, or verifier to manufacture apparent improvement.
- A correctly bound certificate versus changed candidate bytes, changed state,
  stale time, mismatched model, forged receipt, or replayed old approval.
- An exploratory strategy revision versus a persistent executable rewrite;
  exploratory authorization must not silently authorize the latter.
- Different complexity-audit values with identical research inputs: admission,
  scheduling, and switch decisions remain identical. Logging costs may differ
  only when the measurement operation itself genuinely differs.

Formal negative examples should exhibit the missing mathematical hypothesis,
not just malformed JSON. Runtime tests should exercise actual gate boundaries.
Successful tests are evidence about implementation behavior, not a substitute
for the semantic connection required by milestone 3.

## Machine-authored bootstrap and experimental status

The initial input is this design, the user-selected research problem descriptions
and primary-source references, pinned Lean/Mathlib metadata, and a minimal launch
and containment interface. The machine must create the new implementation,
formal statements, proofs, experiments, tests, and documentation. The supervisor
provides execution, resource limits, evidence retention, and independent audit;
it must not insert mathematical solution steps or implement the research engine
on the machine's behalf while describing the result as machine-authored.

A bootstrap cannot claim that its first controller edits are already authorized
by a Gödel switch theorem whose verifier and executable semantics it has yet to
construct. Those edits run in an explicitly experimental workspace under the
user's authorization to rebuild. Compilation, tests, and subsequent independent
checks can validate aspects of the resulting code. They do not retroactively
prove that the bootstrap's sequence of edits was utility-optimal.

The machine must report separate transitions between these statuses:

- **Experimental bootstrap:** code generation and exploration without an
  installed whole-continuation switch certificate.
- **Checked research:** concrete proof objects pass an independently validated
  admission boundary; individual accepted propositions may be reported exactly.
- **Verified model:** formal theorems describe an explicitly stated machine and
  environment model, with the implementation bridge still separately identified.
- **Certified persistent switch:** an actual installation passes the bound,
  independently checked certificate and execution-bridge obligations above.

These labels are evidence classes, not mathematical levels, utility scores,
or a requirement that all components progress in a fixed order. A machine can
produce a valid mathematical theorem during an experimental bootstrap. That
alone certifies neither its surrounding engine nor its future self-modifications.
Machine-generated reports of success remain claims until their evidence is
independently checked; a self-authored test harness cannot certify itself by
printing a successful receipt.

## Clean-input and provenance acceptance checklist

Before the rebuilding proposer runs, independently verify the following:

- Historical source, draft implementations, proof scripts, discoveries, tests,
  experiments, transcripts, and run receipts are archived for the user outside
  the proposer's readable filesystem boundary. They are not bootstrap inputs.
- A Git archive preserves the historical work without exposing its object store
  or archive branch to the proposer. Deleting the working tree while leaving
  `git show` access to earlier solutions does not establish a clean boundary.
- No historical project `.olean`, generated module, cached proof expression,
  database, notebook output, or task-specific package supplies previous results.
  A pinned standard Lean/Mathlib installation is a declared dependency, not
  evidence of a newly created theorem.
- The proposer begins with a fresh conversation. Old assistant summaries,
  hidden solution files, previous success reports, and strategy suggestions
  are not inherited through its prompt, tools, environment, or resume state.
- Task inputs identify the selected publication or conjecture and the required
  outcome. They do not include previously found witnesses, lemmas, reductions,
  or successful representations. Public primary sources remain legitimate
  research inputs and their actual use is recorded.
- The run records an input manifest, hashes, toolchain pins, capabilities,
  workspace boundary, initial prompt, model identity, and resource limits.
  Archived historical objects and fresh generated objects remain distinguishable.
- All new code and mathematical artifacts are traceable to machine actions.
  Any later human correction, imported result, or boundary exception is recorded
  explicitly and narrows the corresponding autonomy or clean-input claim.
- Generated artifacts cannot overwrite supervisor-owned launch rules, hidden
  archives, independent validation tools, evidence manifests, or contract inputs.
  Proposed changes to those components remain candidates for separate review.

A prompt requesting that the proposer ignore readable historical answers is a
behavioral instruction, not enforced clean isolation. If filesystem isolation
is unavailable, report that limitation rather than claiming an enforced clean
run. The archive must remain recoverable by the user; cleaning the proposer
workspace does not authorize loss of the preserved historical work.

## What this specification does not yet establish

No implementation, kernel-checked result, certified controller rewrite, or
resolution of either selected research task is established by this document.
The machine must construct and test the machinery and supply the corresponding
evidence. A general continuation theorem, a useful research result, and a full
executable Gödel switch are separate achievements with separate obligations.

def measure_checkpoint(study, plan, arm, key):
    path = study/'arms'/arm/'observer-outbox'/(key+'.json')
    if not path.exists():
        return {'arm': arm, 'key': key, 'status': 'missing_scheduled_checkpoint',
                'conditional_minimum_proof_complexity': None, 'measured_witness_bytes': None}
    feed = read(path)
    snapshot = study/feed['snapshot']
    manifest = verify_snapshot(snapshot)
    if feed['snapshot_binding'] != manifest['binding'] or digest(feed['mathematics']) != feed['mathematics_binding']:
        raise Invalid('observer binding changed')
    start = time.monotonic()
    data = feed['mathematics']
    prior = read(study/'arms'/arm/'snapshots/initial/manifest.json')['files']
    witnesses, definitions, bridges, residuals = [], {}, {}, []
    all_records = {**data['knowledge'], **data['components']}
    connected = {k for k, v in all_records.items() if v['kind'] == 'reductions'}
    pending = list(connected)
    while pending:
        current = all_records[pending.pop()]
        for dep in current['dependencies']:
            if dep not in connected:
                connected.add(dep)
                pending.append(dep)
    for residual in data['remaining_obligations'].values():
        if residual.get('source') in connected and residual.get('discharge'):
            connected.add(residual['discharge'])
    for identifier in sorted(connected):
        record = all_records[identifier]
        proposal = record['proposal']
        # Exact root reductions and representation transports carry residual
        # proof tasks. Unrelated checked facts remain knowledge, not a shorter goal.
        witnesses.append({'id': record['id'], 'kind': record['kind'], 'task': record['task'],
                          'proposal': proposal, 'receipt_hash': record['receipt_hash']})
        for name, hashed in record['source_files'].items():
            if manifest['files'].get(name) != hashed:
                raise Invalid('witness definitions missing from bound snapshot')
            if prior.get(name) == hashed:
                continue  # explicitly conditional on unchanged initial dictionary
            text = (snapshot/'source'/name).read_text()
            target = bridges if name.endswith(record.get('export_module', '').split('.')[-1]+'.lean') else definitions
            target[name] = text
    for identifier, residual in sorted(data['remaining_obligations'].items()):
        if residual.get('source') not in connected:
            continue
        residuals.append({'id': identifier, **residual,
            'proof_encoding_bytes': None if residual['status'] == 'open' else 'included in checked discharge bundle where available'})
    # Count every new definition/adapter and bridge exactly once, even when an
    # abbreviation makes an individual residual statement shorter.
    bundle = {'encoding': plan['encoding'], 'root': plan['root'], 'panel': plan['panel_hash'],
              'conditional_dictionary': prior, 'witnesses': witnesses, 'definitions': definitions,
              'bridges': bridges, 'residual_tasks': residuals}
    artifact = study/'audit/burden-bundles'/arm/(key+'.json')
    write(artifact, bundle)
    return {'schema': 'math-gkm.cumulative-witness-storage.v2', 'arm': arm, 'key': key,
        'status': 'measured_explicit_witness_with_unknown_residual_burden' if witnesses else 'insufficient_checked_connection',

    """Explicit partial proof descriptions conditioned on each accepted theory.

        'context': {n: sha(study/'seed'/n) for n in seed if n.endswith('.lean')}}] + suite['tasks']
    result = {'schema': 'math-gkm.conditional-remaining.v2', 'arm': arm, 'before': old, 'after': new,
        'reference_tasks': references, 'reference_binding': digest(references),
        'encoding': 'canonical UTF-8 JSON partial Lean application descriptions v2',
        'minimum_proof_complexity': None, 'proof_difficulty_change': None,
        'status': 'audit_only', 'theories': {}}
    dictionaries = {}
    for key in (old, new):
        path = study/'arms'/arm/'observer-outbox'/(key+'.json')

        dictionary = {n: (snap/'source'/n).read_text() for n in sorted(paths)}
        dictionaries[key] = dictionary
        descriptions = []

            for oid, obligation in sorted(data['remaining_obligations'].items()):

                residuals.append({'id': oid, 'exact_target': obligation.get('target_constant'),
                    'context_binding': obligation.get('context_binding'),
                    'checked_discharge_reference': discharge['exports'][0] if discharge else None,
                    'unknown_proof_remainder_bytes': None if not discharge else 0})
            descriptions.append({'target': 'exact-root', 'apply_checked_reduction': record['exports'][0],
                'receipt_hash': record['receipt_hash'], 'residuals': residuals,
                'meaning': 'partial derivation description; holes explicitly unknown'})
        fixed = [{'task': t['id'], 'proof': None, 'unknown_proof_remainder_bytes': None}
                 for t in references if t['id'] != 'exact-root' or not descriptions]
        payload = {'descriptions': descriptions, 'unwitnessed_reference_tasks': fixed}
        result['theories'][key] = {'theory_binding': digest(dictionary),
            'snapshot_binding': manifest['binding'], 'dictionary_source_hashes': {n: digest(v) for n,v in dictionary.items()},
            'conditional_description': payload, 'conditional_description_bytes': len(canonical(payload).encode()),

    removed = sorted(set(dictionaries[old])-set(dictionaries[new]))
    categories = {'dictionary_definitions': {}, 'adapters_and_connecting_proofs': {}}
    for n,text in delta.items():

`raw.json` retains every unfavorable and favorable observation. `burden.svg` plots raw bytes, connects only the same arm/reference-set/data hash, and marks reported representation/strategy changes. `paired-comparisons.json` admits a drop comparison only for exactly two measurements on the same data and reference set. Changed data form separate trajectories. Connecting points is visual ordering, not interpolation evidence.

Raw bytes measure the explicitly named artifact's encoding. zlib level 9 byte counts are also saved, but are not shortest descriptions, Kolmogorov complexity, mathematical difficulty or a reward. Representation semantics and encoding choices may change; a byte drop alone proves no improvement. A sawtooth may be absent. This program neither detects nor manufactures one.

The x coordinate uses the accounting basis recorded per series: manual `measure` sums worker-watchdog wall (including provider wait/tools) and separately run validation wall; retrospective `collect` uses only actual worker receipts completed before a snapshot. These bases never join a trajectory. Neither is CPU, invoice cost, token equivalence or total elapsed calendar time. Measurement overhead is separate. Controller overhead is unknown. Provider usage remains verbatim in receipts. Prediction/transfer results remain in independently checked evaluation records; this byte plot does not imply them. Retrospective bundles measure active Lean source storage against a fixed target, not an encoding of mathematical input data; equivalence is not asserted.

Audit files are outside every live proposer filesystem grant and are absent from the policy/request projection. Do not copy this report or its derived proxies into a research request. Synthetic fixtures are not mathematical evidence.
''')
    return {'records': len(records), 'groups': len(groups), 'synthetic': synthetic, 'output': str(output)}

def collect(study):
    """Post-run observer of immutable snapshots; never called by the controller.

    The representation is an exact canonical JSON source bundle, not a compressed
    encoding of mathematical data. The fixed reference is the pinned target file.
    Reconstruct costs only from actual receipts ending before each snapshot.
    """
    collected = []
    for arm in ('baseline', 'exploration'):
        root = study/'arms'/arm
        receipts = [read(p) for p in (root/'jobs').glob('*/receipt.json')]
        previous_policy = None
        for path in sorted((root/'snapshots').iterdir()):
            manifest = verify_snapshot(path)
            start = time.monotonic()
            sources = {name: (path/'source'/name).read_text() for name in sorted(manifest['files'])
                       if name.startswith('MathGKM/') and name.endswith('.lean')}
            bundle = study/'audit/bundles'/f'{arm}-{path.name}.json'
            write(bundle, sources)
            raw = bundle.read_bytes()
            cost = sum(r.get('elapsed_seconds', 0) for r in receipts
                       if r.get('finished', float('inf')) <= manifest['created'])
            marker = 'initial representation' if previous_policy is None else (
                'strategy change' if previous_policy != manifest['policy'] else None)
            previous_policy = manifest['policy']
            record = {'schema': 'math-gkm.audit.v2', 'synthetic': read(study/'protocol.json')['transport'] == 'fixture',
                'arm': arm, 'artifact': str(bundle), 'artifact_sha256': sha(bundle),
                'dataset_sha256': sha(study/'seed/MathGKM/Markov.lean'), 'reference_set': 'fixed-pinned-target-source',
                'representation': 'canonical active MathGKM source bundle at '+path.name,
                'pair_id': None, 'marker': marker, 'raw_bytes': len(raw), 'zlib9_bytes': len(zlib.compress(raw, 9)),
                'cumulative_research_seconds': cost, 'timestamp': manifest['created'],
                'cost_basis': 'worker_wall_only_before_snapshot',
                'measurement_seconds': time.monotonic()-start,
                'cost': {'accounting': 'Only actual worker/watchdog wall completed before snapshot; excludes standalone validation and controller wall. Unknown interrupted receipts excluded, not treated as observed zero.',
                         'subprocess_wall_seconds': cost, 'validation_wall_seconds': None,
                         'controller_overhead_seconds': None},
                'meaning': 'Exact active Lean source bundle storage against fixed target bytes; excludes archived sources and non-Lean experiments. No claim that programs are equivalent or encode the dataset; no prediction/transfer inference.'}
            write(study/'audit/raw'/f'collected-{arm}-{path.name}.json', record)
            collected.append(record)
    return {'observations': len(collected), 'status': 'audit_only; no decisions affected'}

def main():
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    sub = p.add_subparsers(dest='command', required=True)
    plot = sub.add_parser('report')
    plot.add_argument('--study', type=Path, required=True)
    plot.add_argument('--output', type=Path, required=True)
    c = sub.add_parser('collect')
    c.add_argument('--study', type=Path, required=True)
    m = sub.add_parser('measure')
    m.add_argument('--study', type=Path, required=True)
    m.add_argument('--arm', choices=['baseline', 'exploration'], required=True)
    for flag in ('artifact', 'dataset'):
        m.add_argument('--'+flag, type=Path, required=True)
    for flag in ('reference-set', 'representation'):
        m.add_argument('--'+flag, required=True)
    m.add_argument('--marker')
    m.add_argument('--pair-id')
    a = p.parse_args()
    if a.command == 'collect':
        result = collect(a.study.resolve())
    elif a.command == 'report':
        result = report(a.study.resolve(), a.output.resolve())
    else:
        result = measure(a.study.resolve(), a.arm, a.artifact, a.dataset, a.reference_set, a.representation, a.marker, a.pair_id)
    print(canonical(result))

if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

The fixed encoding is a canonical source/term/task bundle with the pinned Lean
rebuild/replay decoder. Only a checked witness has a measured encoding. Unknown
residual proofs remain unknown; no search failure gives a lower bound. This is

import argparse

def measure_checkpoint(study, plan, arm, key):
    path = study/'arms'/arm/'observer-outbox'/(key+'.json')
    if not path.exists():
        return {'arm': arm, 'key': key, 'status': 'missing_scheduled_checkpoint',
                'conditional_minimum_proof_complexity': None, 'measured_witness_bytes': None}
    feed = read(path)
    snapshot = study/feed['snapshot']
    manifest = verify_snapshot(snapshot)
    if feed['snapshot_binding'] != manifest['binding'] or digest(feed['mathematics']) != feed['mathematics_binding']:
        raise Invalid('observer binding changed')
    start = time.monotonic()
    data = feed['mathematics']
    prior = read(study/'arms'/arm/'snapshots/initial/manifest.json')['files']
    witnesses, definitions, bridges, residuals = [], {}, {}, []
    all_records = {**data['knowledge'], **data['components']}
    connected = {k for k, v in all_records.items() if v['kind'] == 'reductions'}
    pending = list(connected)
    while pending:
        current = all_records[pending.pop()]
        for dep in current['dependencies']:
            if dep not in connected:
                connected.add(dep)
                pending.append(dep)
    for residual in data['remaining_obligations'].values():
        if residual.get('source') in connected and residual.get('discharge'):
            connected.add(residual['discharge'])
    for identifier in sorted(connected):
        record = all_records[identifier]
        proposal = record['proposal']
        # Exact root reductions and representation transports carry residual
        # proof tasks. Unrelated checked facts remain knowledge, not a shorter goal.
        witnesses.append({'id': record['id'], 'kind': record['kind'], 'task': record['task'],
                          'proposal': proposal, 'receipt_hash': record['receipt_hash']})
        for name, hashed in record['source_files'].items():
            if manifest['files'].get(name) != hashed:
                raise Invalid('witness definitions missing from bound snapshot')
            if prior.get(name) == hashed:
                continue  # explicitly conditional on unchanged initial dictionary
            text = (snapshot/'source'/name).read_text()
            target = bridges if name.endswith(record.get('export_module', '').split('.')[-1]+'.lean') else definitions
            target[name] = text
    for identifier, residual in sorted(data['remaining_obligations'].items()):
        if residual.get('source') not in connected:
            continue
        residuals.append({'id': identifier, **residual,
            'proof_encoding_bytes': None if residual['status'] == 'open' else 'included in checked discharge bundle where available'})
    # Count every new definition/adapter and bridge exactly once, even when an
    # abbreviation makes an individual residual statement shorter.
    bundle = {'encoding': plan['encoding'], 'root': plan['root'], 'panel': plan['panel_hash'],
              'conditional_dictionary': prior, 'witnesses': witnesses, 'definitions': definitions,
              'bridges': bridges, 'residual_tasks': residuals}
    artifact = study/'audit/burden-bundles'/arm/(key+'.json')
    write(artifact, bundle)
    return {'schema': 'math-gkm.cumulative-witness-storage.v2', 'arm': arm, 'key': key,
        'status': 'measured_explicit_witness_with_unknown_residual_burden' if witnesses else 'insufficient_checked_connection',
        'root': plan['root'], 'panel_hash': plan['panel_hash'], 'encoding': plan['encoding'],
        'snapshot_binding': manifest['binding'], 'bundle_sha256': sha(artifact),

        'definition_dictionary_bytes': len(canonical(definitions).encode()),

    result = {'schema': 'math-gkm.conditional-remaining.v2', 'arm': arm, 'before': old, 'after': new,
        'reference_tasks': references, 'reference_binding': digest(references),
        'encoding': 'canonical UTF-8 JSON partial Lean application descriptions v2',
        'minimum_proof_complexity': None, 'proof_difficulty_change': None,
        'status': 'audit_only', 'theories': {}}

        paths |= {n for r in records.values() for n in r['source_files']}
        dictionary = {n: (snap/'source'/n).read_text() for n in sorted(paths)}
        dictionaries[key] = dictionary
        descriptions = []
        for rid, record in sorted(records.items()):
            if record['kind'] != 'reductions':
                continue
            residuals = []
            for oid, obligation in sorted(data['remaining_obligations'].items()):
                if obligation.get('source') != rid:
                    continue
                discharge = records.get(obligation.get('discharge'))
                residuals.append({'id': oid, 'exact_target': obligation.get('target_constant'),
                    'context_binding': obligation.get('context_binding'),
                    'checked_discharge_reference': discharge['exports'][0] if discharge else None,
                    'unknown_proof_remainder_bytes': None if not discharge else 0})
            descriptions.append({'target': 'exact-root', 'apply_checked_reduction': record['exports'][0],
                'receipt_hash': record['receipt_hash'], 'residuals': residuals,
                'meaning': 'partial derivation description; holes explicitly unknown'})
        fixed = [{'task': t['id'], 'proof': None, 'unknown_proof_remainder_bytes': None}
                 for t in references if t['id'] != 'exact-root' or not descriptions]
        payload = {'descriptions': descriptions, 'unwitnessed_reference_tasks': fixed}
        result['theories'][key] = {'theory_binding': digest(dictionary),
            'snapshot_binding': manifest['binding'], 'dictionary_source_hashes': {n: digest(v) for n,v in dictionary.items()},
            'conditional_description': payload, 'conditional_description_bytes': len(canonical(payload).encode()),
            'unknown_proof_remainder': 'unknown; missing proofs are never assigned zero bytes',

    removed = sorted(set(dictionaries[old])-set(dictionaries[new]))
    categories = {'dictionary_definitions': {}, 'adapters_and_connecting_proofs': {}}
    for n,text in delta.items():
        category = 'adapters_and_connecting_proofs' if '/Accepted' in n or '/Target' in n else 'dictionary_definitions'

    result.update(enlargement=not removed and all(dictionaries[new].get(n) == t for n,t in dictionaries[old].items()),
        removed_or_changed_old_sources=[n for n,t in dictionaries[old].items() if dictionaries[new].get(n) != t],

        overhead_bytes={k: len(canonical(v).encode()) for k,v in categories.items()},
        shared_cost_rule='Each new source appears once across overhead categories; dictionary is not a free abbreviation.',
        interpretation='Same exact reference tasks under two bound theories. Description bytes are not proof difficulty; no forced change.')

Only bound mathematical state, witness sources and accounting are exported.
No observer output is read by this module or any research/control role.

from .study_common import Invalid, digest, read, write, verify_snapshot


def checkpoint(study, arm, key, state, snapshot):
    manifest = verify_snapshot(snapshot)
    research = state['research']
    mathematical = {k: research.get(k, {}) for k in ('knowledge', 'components', 'remaining_obligations')}
    mathematical['program'] = research['program']
    mathematical['policy'] = research['policy']
    record = {'schema': 'math-gkm.observer-input.v1', 'key': key, 'arm': arm,
        'snapshot': str(snapshot.relative_to(study)), 'snapshot_binding': manifest['binding'],
        'mathematics': mathematical, 'mathematics_binding': digest(mathematical),
        'reservation_seconds': state['seconds'],
        'worker_observed_seconds': sum(read(p+'/receipt.json').get('elapsed_seconds', 0) for p in state['receipts']),
        'controller_active_seconds': state.get('controller_active_seconds', 0),
        'accounting': 'Reservations are caps, not measured cost; controller active wall overlaps subprocess wall. Never sum overlapping totals.',
        'created': manifest['created']}
    target = study/'audit/inputs'/arm/(key+'.json')
    # Research-owned durable outbox; audit-side values never gate execution.
    outbox = study/'arms'/arm/'observer-outbox'/(key+'.json')
    if not outbox.exists():
        write(outbox, record)
    else:
        record = read(outbox)
    if not target.exists():
        write(target, record)
    else:
        write(study/'audit/reconciliations'/arm/(key+'-'+digest(record)+'.json'), record)
    return record
"""Use the strengthened exact-root verifier with explicit workspace binding.

The legacy source-to-root and independent correspondence requirements are not
weakened. Fixture transport cannot resolve mathematics, even with a fake audit.
"""
import argparse
from pathlib import Path
import time
from . import completion
from .study_common import Invalid, read, write, canonical, lock, digest
from .study import Arm, verify
from .study_transfer import sandbox_prefix, dependency_paths

def check(arm, claim, audit=None):
    if arm.p['transport'] == 'fixture':
        return {'resolved': False, 'rejection': 'fixture can never resolve mathematics'}
    seconds = arm.p['validation_seconds']
    key = digest({'claim': claim, 'audit': audit, 'round': arm.s['round']})
    directory = arm.root/'completion'/key
    if (directory/'result.json').exists():
        result = read(directory/'result.json')
        # A result file is written during validation too. Only a finished exact
        # bundle may be reused, and resolution survives recovery.
        if 'finished' not in result:
            raise Invalid('interrupted completion validation; never replayed')
        old_root = completion.ROOT
        try:
            completion.ROOT = arm.workspace
            if completion.prepare(read(arm.workspace/'contract.json'), claim)['bundle_hash'] != result.get('bundle_hash'):
                raise Invalid('completion bundle changed since checked receipt')
        finally:
            completion.ROOT = old_root
        if result['resolved']:
            arm.s.update(resolution=result, status='mathematically_resolved')
            arm.save()
            terminal(arm)
        return result
    if directory.exists():
        raise Invalid('interrupted completion validation; new independently reviewed attempt required')
    arm.reserve('completion-'+key, seconds)
    directory.mkdir(parents=True)
    start = time.monotonic()
    old_root, old_run = completion.ROOT, completion.run
    prefix = sandbox_prefix(directory, dependency_paths(arm.workspace))
    def bounded(argv, **kwargs):
        remaining = seconds - (time.monotonic()-start)
        if remaining <= 0:
            raise completion.Rejected('failure within completion validation budget')
        kwargs['timeout'] = min(kwargs['timeout'], remaining)
        kwargs['env'] = {**kwargs['env'], 'TMPDIR': str(directory)}
        return old_run(prefix+argv, **kwargs)
    try:
        completion.ROOT = arm.workspace
        completion.run = bounded
        result = completion.verify(read(arm.workspace/'contract.json'), claim, directory,
                                   audit=audit, stop=arm.stopped)
    finally:
        completion.ROOT, completion.run = old_root, old_run
    if result['resolved']:
        arm.s['resolution'] = result
        arm.s['status'] = 'mathematically_resolved'
        arm.save()
        terminal(arm)
    return result


def terminal(arm):
    from .study_common import snapshot
    from .study_observer import checkpoint
    target = arm.root/'snapshots/terminal'
    if not target.exists():
        snapshot(arm.workspace, target, arm.s['research']['policy'], arm.admitted(arm.s['research']))
    checkpoint(arm.study, arm.mode, 'terminal', arm.s, target)

def main():
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    p.add_argument('--study', type=Path, required=True)
    p.add_argument('--arm', choices=['baseline', 'exploration'], required=True)
    p.add_argument('--claim', type=Path, required=True)
    p.add_argument('--audit', type=Path)
    a = p.parse_args()
    directory = a.study.resolve()
    verify(directory)
    with lock(directory/'controller.lock') as fd:
        result = check(Arm(directory, a.arm, fd), read(a.claim), read(a.audit) if a.audit else None)
    print(canonical(result))

if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()
